findings.text: Kept as an advisory (Q2), as in round 6. The findings file and the code have not changed. The card tests change.old against its own /^mute/ to pick its fallback name. That repeats, more loosely, the mute grammar that serverChange in ui/src/sharing-text.ts already parses, and only the leaf has a test. The text shown is still right, so this is a maintenance risk, not a defect.

Kept as an advisory (Q1/Q5), carried by the reviewer from round 6. Nothing tests that the card calls serverChange, the name it passes, or the fallback name for a server no longer listed. The rubric calls a coverage gap like this advisory, and the shown text is in the captures. Round 6's only defect is gone. It was tests/unit/ui-sharing-copy.test.ts:99, filed against AC-85 (preserve). I checked work.json: line 883 records a skip of tdd:AC-85 by the user, and D-10 (work.json:1097) retires AC-85 in favour of AC-92. So AC-85 is no longer a live criterion. The verdict reads AC-92 (observed), and its scope names the changes in that file: the saveSettings call, the signature regexes, and the Servers and dock cases. probes/criteria.md:13 still lists AC-85 because the file was not regenerated. That gap is in the record only and fails no rubric question on a line of the diff. The reviewer's other carried advisory, round 5's whole-file class search, names no line this round, so I give no separate ruling on it.

Kept as an advisory (public-api). Unchanged since round 5. Pull-page items get no shape check where they enter, and the answer body has no size cap. Path parts are checked, entry uids go through the strict parseEntryUid, and an item that throws is set aside.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). Unchanged. A received memory is filed under any enabled project that holds the alias, with no aliasBoundTo check. The brief and the prompt keep the row out, and only the receiving member can see it.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). Unchanged. Received memories become ordinary rows. memory_search and the consolidation neighbours apply no mute or binding check, and the diff did not write those readers. This is debt.

Kept as an advisory (personal-data). Unchanged. After a restore, the copies of a server no longer listed are deleted only when someone runs sync --once by hand, and the CLI tells the person to run it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). Unchanged. --code on the command line puts the invitation code in shell history and ps. A no-echo prompt exists, and the usage text names it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). Unchanged. remove forgets the token only on this machine, and the person is told that the device stays valid until an admin revokes it.
Kept as an advisory (auth). Unchanged. The resume and add confirmations act on the state at the moment of the yes, not on the preview the person saw. Nothing beyond the policy is sent.

Kept as an advisory. The Rejoin code field is a password input outside a form, which produces log:verbose entries only (review/ui/console-settings-rejoining.json, review/ui/settings-rejoining@1280-dark.png), and Enter does not submit. Q10 holds, as the reviewer says. This is a small affordance gap, not a defect.

Kept as an advisory, as in rounds 3 to 6. The held state is declared and captured (review/ui/settings-held@1280-light.png, review/ui/settings-held@360-dark.png). Only holdLine's branch with n withdrawals and resumeDescription's per-project lines have no capture, and neither is a declared state the manifest lists as missing. The empty-hold wording, which states the result before the action, is a copy nit.

Kept as an advisory, as in rounds 4 to 6. Stale toasts stack across the states (review/ui/settings-listed@360-light.png, review/ui/settings-confirming@1280-light.png), but they hide no control any state needs.

Kept as an advisory. The reviewer files this as cosmetic: Remove… and Rejoin… open a plain modal, while Resume… opens the Confirm shape with an icon (review/ui/settings-removing@768-light.png, review/ui/settings-resuming@768-dark.png). Both read clearly.

Kept as an advisory (Q1/Q4). Unchanged since round 2. The 'held pull answered at once' rule measures the time since the last answer, not how long the request was held, so the back-off does not double as spec.md:187 says. The server's own hold limits the loop, and status shows the last error.
Kept as an advisory (Q1). Unchanged. INDEXED BY sharing_memories_updated fails on a store that lacks the index. ADR 0027:87 limits this to unreleased development stores.

Kept as an advisory (Q1). Carried unchanged from round 2. The sync runs its own SQL over the knowledge module's tables, and no boundary test guards that coupling. The base draws no explicit rule that this breaks.
Kept as an advisory (Q3). Carried unchanged from round 2. RESULT_SHAPES.refusal leaves out the optional accepted and retryAfterSec keys that RefusalShape declares and the client reads.
